input.quote: Ono shall, and shall require its Affiliates to, permit Array, and/or an authorized representative reasonably acceptable to Ono, to enter the relevant facilities of Ono and its Affiliates during normal business hours and upon reasonable advance notice to inspect and verify compliance with applicable regulatory and other requirements, as well as with this Agreement
input.rationale: Two clauses give Array verification rights against Ono. Section 7.4 (p0481-p0483) is close to the fallback: once each Calendar Year, independent accounting firm reasonably acceptable to Ono, confidentiality undertaking, Array's expense — but the notice is only "reasonable prior written notice" and the underpayment cost-shift threshold is left blank ("[ * ]"), so neither the 15-day notice nor the 10% cost trigger is secured. Section 4.9 (p0359) is the material failure: Array (or its representative) may enter Ono's facilities and examine internal procedures and records on merely "reasonable advance notice" with no frequency limit at all, which is unlimited-audit walk-away territory and survives termination (p0674). We therefore target the fallback: a once-per-year cap and 15 days' prior written notice on the 4.9 inspection, 15 days' notice on the 7.4 records inspection, and the cost threshold fixed at 10% underpayment. We did not press the preferred position (independent auditor, off-site, no facility access) for Section 4.9 because removing the on-site regulatory-compliance inspection would require collateral rewrites of the GxP regime in Article IV.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.

proposal.summary: Add a once-per-year cap and 15 days' notice to Array's inspection rights and fix the audit-cost threshold at 10% underpayment.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept Array's inspection and audit rights, but they need the usual guardrails: a once-per-year cap and at least 15 days' prior written notice for the Section 4.9 facility inspection (today it is unlimited in frequency on merely "reasonable" notice), the same 15 days' notice for the Section 7.4 records inspection, and confirmation that Array bears inspection costs unless an underpayment exceeds 10%.
